name: Dishonored
body:
A dishonored is a vanguard that eschews their code and their responsibilities and can be the bane of the protectors of the realm or simply errant warriors selling their skills to the highest bidder.

Special: The dishonored may be an archetype that the vanguard gains during their career, in this case the archetype is added at the time and all the abilities are replaced. In this instance, if the vanguard has an archetype, this archetype is applied over the top and replaces those abilities with the exception of the mercenary captain or templar archetypes. Those two archetypes are not compatible with this archetype. The mercenary captain is not one to be dishonored and the templar has their own rules for losing their abilities. If at a later date, the vanguard atones for their actions either via the atonement spell or by other means at the GM’s discretion, the vanguard may resume their original vanguard or archetype and lose the replacements given by this archetype.

Alignment: The dishonored may not be lawful. If the dishonored was previously lawful, their alignment must have shifted.

Code: The dishonored is not bound to a code of conduct but they have an intense belief in their own prowess. If they are defeated while using the test of valor or trial by combat abilities, their maximum mettle is reduced by 1 for 24 hours. This ability modifies code but are usable with archetypes that modify the code.

Mettle: The dishonored may not gain Mettle points back from successfully aiding another in a skill check or successfully improving their AC. This ability modifies mettle but may be used with other archetypes that modify or replace mettle.

Selfish Defense (Ex)

Any ability used by the dishonored that may be used to defend another or the dishonored, the ability only applies to the dishonored.

For example, valorous deflection only benefits the dishonored and ever vigilant does not provide any benefit to allies. This ability modifies any ability given by the vanguard or an archetype.

Underhanded Tactics (Ex)

At 3rd level, the dishonored gains a bonus to dirty trick combat maneuvers equal to 1/2 their class level and such maneuvers do not provoke attacks of opportunity.

Additionally, the dishonored gains a sneak attack equal to 1d6 per 4 class levels they have.

This ability replaces behind me or any archetype ability that replaced or modified behind me.

Scatter the Cowards (Ex)

At 8th level, the dishonored may expend a point of Mettle as a move action to use Intimidate to demoralize all enemies within 60 feet. The targeted enemies must be able to see or hear the dishonored. If the successfully demoralized targets are already shaken, they are instead frightened.

This demoralizing effect lasts for 1d6 rounds, rolled separately for each target. The dishonored gain a bonus on this Intimidate check equal to 1/2 their class level.

Any enemy may only be affected by this ability once in any 24 hour period.

At 13th level, the condition lasts until the end of combat and any enemy that has their demoralize DC defeated by 5 or more, is frightened instead of shaken or panicked if already frightened or shaken. Any frightened or panicked condition imposed by this ability lasts for 1 minute. After the minute, the target is no longer frightened or panicked but remain shaken for the remainder of combat.

At 16th level, the ability may be activated as a swift action and any enemy with HD more than 5 less than the dishonored automatically is frightened or panicked if the demoralize attempt succeeds.

This ability replaces call to action, to arms and overwhelming presence or any archetype ability that replaces those abilities.

Scourge of the Realm (Ex)

At 20th level, the dishonored gains an aura of their alignment as a cleric of the same level. Any weapon they wield is treated as chaotically-aligned, people of the lower classes or criminal elements always have a starting attitude of at least indifferent to the dishonored unless they have been given direct orders to oppose them or it would be extremely beneficial for them to do so, and lastly, they no longer need to expend Mettle to activate test of valor and trial by combat, these abilities only require the dishonored to spend the action the ability requires.

This ability replaces protector of the realm or any ability that modifies or replaces protector of the realm.
